title_en: Zhou Kaifeng et al. v. Yichang County Construction Bureau — dispute over compensation for personal injury
keywords_en: Civil; Personal injury damages; First instance; Basic People's Court; Hubei Province; Natural person; State organ; General Principles of Civil Law; Determination of employment relationship versus contract for services; Application of the principle of fairness; Partial support; Hanging banners; Death from falling from a building; Breakage of skylight glass; Principle of fairness
full_text_en:
Zhou Kaifeng et al. v. Yichang County Construction Bureau — dispute over compensation for personal injury

Plaintiff: Zhou Kaifeng, female, 29 years old, unemployed, residing at the Jinshi Hotel dormitory in Yichang County, Hubei Province.

Plaintiff: He Hao, male, 6 years old, same address.

Legal representative: Zhou Kaifeng, mother of He Hao.

Plaintiff: Kong Fanying, female, 59 years old, unemployed, residing in Wangdian Town, Dangyang City, Hubei Province.

Agent ad litem for the three plaintiffs: Liu Jinfa, lawyer of Hubei Yichang Guangda Law Firm.

Defendant: Hubei Province Yichang County Construction Bureau.

Legal representative: Liu Xianming, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Chen Shoubang, lawyer of Hubei Yichang Guangda Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Deng Keyin, male, official of Hubei Province Yichang County Construction Bureau.

Defendant: He Liping, female, 34 years old, native of Dangyang City, Hubei Province, proprietor of Yichang County Xiaoxita Liping Store, residing at the Jinshi Hotel dormitory in Yichang County.

Agent ad litem: Feng Faqiang, husband of He Liping.

The plaintiffs Zhou Kaifeng, He Hao, and Kong Fanying filed a lawsuit with the Yichang County People's Court of Hubei Province against the defendant Hubei Province Yichang County Construction Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Construction Bureau) concerning a dispute over compensation for personal injury. The court found that He Liping had an interest in the case and added her as a co-defendant.

The three plaintiffs alleged: He Tao was the husband of plaintiff Zhou Kaifeng, the father of plaintiff He Hao, and the son of plaintiff Kong Fanying. On February 19, 1999, He Tao was employed by the defendant Construction Bureau to hang banners. During the work, no one from the Construction Bureau provided assistance, causing He Tao, unaware of the actual conditions, to step through a skylight on the third-floor platform and fall to his death. There was an employment relationship between the Construction Bureau and He Tao. The Construction Bureau was at fault for He Tao's death and should, according to law, bear the employer's liability. The plaintiffs requested the court to order the Construction Bureau to pay them compensation for death, funeral expenses, living expenses for dependents, rescue expenses, expert consultation fees, transportation costs, etc., totaling RMB 72,953.50.

The defendant Construction Bureau argued: It was the defendant He Liping who undertook the banner printing and hanging work from the County Party Committee Propaganda Department and then hired He Tao to complete it. He Tao's accidental fall and death should be the responsibility of the employer He Liping, and the Bureau should not bear any legal liability.

The defendant He Liping argued: I neither undertook the banner printing and hanging work nor hired He Tao to do it. I only helped the three plaintiffs settle the account with the defendant Construction Bureau after He Tao's death. I have no legal interest in this dispute.

The Yichang County People's Court of Hubei Province found through trial:

In January 1999, the Yichang County Committee of the Communist Party of China decided to hold a "four-level" cadre conference and required all units to hang banners during the conference. After learning this, Feng Faqiang, the husband of defendant He Liping, contacted the County Party Committee Propaganda Department and requested that the task of making and hanging banners be assigned to He Liping and her younger brother He Tao. The Propaganda Department agreed that they could contact the units themselves and settle the costs themselves. He Tao, under the title of General Manager of the "Damin Craft Decoration Company" (which had not undergone industrial and commercial registration and had no fixed personnel), holding the "Notice on Seriously Doing a Good Job of Hanging Propaganda Banners for the County Four-Level Cadre Conference" issued by the Propaganda Department, approached various units to negotiate banner printing and hanging matters. After negotiations with the defendant Construction Bureau, the Construction Bureau agreed that He Tao would print one new banner as required by the document and be responsible for hanging two banners (including an old one) at a price of RMB 800.

On the morning of February 19, 1999, He Tao, together with his hired assistants Cheng Zhixin and Cheng Zhiming, took the newly made banner to the defendant Construction Bureau. They were allowed into the office building by the duty personnel Li Zhimin and Zhang Jianjun. Li Zhimin accompanied He Tao and the other two to the twelfth floor to retrieve the old banner placed there. After fixing the tops of the two banners to the roof, He Tao and the others threw the banners down. The wooden pole at the lower end of the left banner got stuck on the third-floor platform. He Tao and Cheng Zhixin then went down to the third floor. The third-floor platform was made of skylight glass, covered with excessive dust. Observing the platform from the third-floor corridor, He Tao assumed it was a cement slab. He jumped from the women's restroom window onto the platform. Stepping through the skylight glass, He Tao fell to the first floor, sustaining severe injuries, and died despite rescue efforts. After He Tao's death, defendant He Liping used an invoice from her individually operated Liping Store to settle the account of RMB 800 with the defendant Construction Bureau and turned the money over to the three plaintiffs.

On July 14, 1999, He Tao's wife Zhou Kaifeng, son He Hao, and mother Kong Fanying filed a lawsuit, requesting the defendant Construction Bureau to pay compensation for death of RMB 32,850, funeral expenses of RMB 5,280, living expenses for dependent He Hao of RMB 32,850, rescue expenses of RMB 673.50, expert consultation fees of RMB 200, and transportation costs of RMB 1,100, totaling RMB 72,953.50.

The above facts are confirmed by the "2.19" death accident investigation report, witness statements of Cheng Zhixin, Cheng Zhiming, Li Zhimin, Xi Daizheng, Zhang Jianjun, and Liu Xin, medical expense receipts, Document Yi Xuan Xuan Wen (1999) No. 4, the individual industrial and commercial household registration form, an invoice for printing cloth banners, and the court testimony of witnesses Xi Daizheng and Li Zhimin, as well as the statements of the parties in court and their cross-examination. The evidence is sufficient for identification.

The Yichang County People's Court of Hubei Province held:

He Tao, claiming to be an operator, reached an oral agreement with the defendant Construction Bureau regarding the printing and hanging of banners, forming a legal relationship of work contract between the parties. The Construction Bureau was the ordering party, and He Tao was the contractor. Although the contractor completes the predetermined work for the ordering party, he is not employed by the ordering party; therefore, no employment relationship was formed. He Tao's printing and hanging of the banners were his obligations as a contractor. During the hanging process, He Tao mistakenly judged the dust-covered skylight glass to be a cement platform based on common sense, leading to the accident of falling to his death. Neither He Tao nor the Construction Bureau was at fault for the occurrence of the death. Article 132 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If neither party is at fault for the damage, the civil liability may be shared by the parties according to the actual circumstances." He Tao suffered the damage while providing services to the Construction Bureau. The Construction Bureau may, based on the principle of fairness, provide appropriate compensation. The claim of the three plaintiffs that an employment relationship existed between He Tao and the Construction Bureau, and that He Tao's injury during work should be compensated by the employer Construction Bureau, cannot be established according to law.

Defendant He Liping did not participate in the operation of the "Damin Craft Decoration Company" claimed by He Tao, nor did she hire He Tao for the operation. She only issued an invoice from her Liping Store to settle the account for the plaintiffs after He Tao's death. Therefore, He Liping should not bear civil liability in this case. The defendant Construction Bureau's argument that defendant He Liping undertook the banner printing and hanging work from the County Party Committee Propaganda Department and then hired He Tao to carry it out, and thus the employer He Liping should bear the liability for He Tao's death, contradicts the facts and his defense is not supported. Accordingly, the Yichang County People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 10, 2000:

The defendant Construction Bureau shall pay the plaintiffs Zhou Kaifeng, He Hao, and Kong Fanying economic losses of RMB 29,182.80.

Court costs of RMB 3,844 shall be borne by the defendant Construction Bureau in the amount of RMB 1,922 and by the plaintiffs Zhou Kaifeng, He Hao, and Kong Fanying in the amount of RMB 1,922.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
